title: Tricks for the Parlour
summary: For birthdays and long winter evenings. — Aunt Philippa

pages.text: Close the hand {~around the coin~} and open it on the word; the coin is behind the ear of {~whoever laughs first~}.
Stir three times {~widdershins~}. The cup sings {~for as long as it is warm~}.
Fold the paper into a moth {~with the crease toward you~}. It flies once around the room {~and lands on the cake~}.
Draw the face you want {~on the glass~} and breathe it onto your own. It holds {~until sunset~}, {~or longer if you forget it is there~}.
pages.authorNote: Outlier. A child's accident, and a con artist's tool.

pages.text: A pinch in the candle {~gives green, then blue~}, then {~a colour nobody has a name for~}.
